name: Solgrip Mango-Cardamom Pulls
manufacturer: Solgrip Candy Works (Tier 1-2 street brand, Ward 6)
description: Long, individually wrapped pull-candy strips in bright orange, made with synth-mango flavoring and a cardamom-spiced sugar base. Solgrip uses a mechanical pull process that gives the candy its characteristic airy, stretchy texture — a tactile experience that's become part of the brand identity.
flavor_profile: Sweet, ripe mango with a warm cardamom undercurrent and a slightly floral finish — chewy and aromatic
cultural_context: A Shelf and Tier 1 staple, especially among younger residents. The long strips are often shared — torn in half between friends — making them a minor social currency in tight communities. Street vendors in Ward 6 sell them loose from dispensary drums.
story_hooks: Solgrip Candy Works is one of the only businesses on a contested Ward 6 block that hasn't been bought out by a Corponation development arm — the owner is using the candy shop as a de facto community organizing space.
A Tier 1 teenager has been leaving knotted Solgrip wrappers at specific locations as a gang-neutral signal system — a code that neither local enforcement nor rival crews have decoded yet.

The Solgrip pull machine breaks down and replacement parts are discontinued — the owner has to decide between closing, finding a black-market fabricator, or accepting help from a Corponation that wants a piece of the brand.
